A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Object-Anagram and Configural Shape Score (CSS) study. Text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the added sections and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original model benchmarking, human behavioral results, attention ablations, representational analyses, and correlations with other shape-dependent evaluations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds positional-encoding comparisons, cumulative attention ablations, and evaluation on an expanded anagram set.

M1.justification: The anagram synthesis procedure, patch configuration, category mapping, and joint two-image CSS definition remain unchanged. The positional-encoding variants and cumulative ablations are diagnostic experiments, rather than revisions to the proposed benchmark procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same nine-category anagram task and auxiliary shape-dependent benchmarks. Appendix A.10 expands the anagram sample from 72 to 1,440 pairs without documenting new categories, domains, or task requirements; this changes sample size rather than coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Section 7 and Table 1 add five ViT-B/16 comparators: relative positional embeddings, RoPE, RoPE plus absolute embeddings, mixed RoPE, and mixed RoPE plus absolute embeddings. The original model comparisons remain; Appendix A.11 documents the existing cohort rather than establishing another newly evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: v3 adds evaluation of all 86 models on 1,440 anagram pairs and cumulative masking of blocks before or after a selected layer across four DINOv2 sizes and the ViT-B/16 baseline. These substantially extend sample size and intervention design beyond the retained original evaluation and single-block ablations.

E4.justification: New analyses test positional-encoding effects, whether later layers recover information disrupted by cumulative attention masking, and whether CSS rankings depend on the original small stimulus sample. Section 7 and Appendices A.5 and A.10 substantially extend the existing mechanistic and robustness evidence.

E5.justification: The one-tailed Williams tests over 86 models, including their statistics and p-values, are unchanged between v1 Appendix A.6 and v3 Appendix A.7. No study-specific repeated-run counts, seed reporting, uncertainty definitions, or significance-testing procedures are added; the checklist's generic guidance does not establish such changes.

E6.justification: v3 Table 1 newly reports CSS values of 38.89%, 51.38%, 51.38%, 48.61%, and 52.77% for the five positional-encoding variants. Figures 7 and 11 add cumulative-ablation similarity profiles and expanded-set scores, with original-versus-expanded CSS correlation r=0.99. These are substantial additional results under new configurations or samples; the original reported results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The synthesis equations, CSS definition and chance level, representational-influence definitions, and accuracy-corrected shape-bias formula are retained. No new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or mathematical corrections accompany the added experiments.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and concluding contribution summary retain the same central claims about CSS, differences across models, long-range integration, BagNet controls, and prediction of other evaluations. The additions support and elaborate these claims rather than redefine the main contribution.

C2.justification: v3 discusses possible distribution effects from the black-paint texture and argues that successful individual-image classification points toward configural failure. It also elaborates local-to-global consistency objectives versus reconstruction-based learning and interprets cumulative ablations as identifying irrecoverable intermediate-layer contributions. These refine the existing mechanistic account.

D1.justification: Appendix A.11 substantially expands model documentation beyond v1's family-level descriptions, listing architectures, adversarial-training epsilon values, sparsity levels, register variants, pretraining notes, and input resolutions. The new checklist also states that code and data release is planned; it does not establish completed release.

R1.justification: The related-work section and all 70 references are retained. The positioning of CSS relative to shape-versus-texture bias and earlier configural-shape research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 inserts a positional-encoding section, three appendix subsections, additional discussion, and a conference checklist, while preserving nearly all existing prose and its narrative order. Contact information, conference identification, and cross-references receive limited updates rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v3 substantially extends the visual evidence with cumulative-ablation Figure 7, expanded-set validation Figure 11, positional-encoding Table 1, and the model inventory. Figure 11 also redisplays original scores. All nine original figure images are retained, while the auxiliary-evaluation schematic and statistical table are resized or reformatted.

improvement.justification: v1's central benchmark conclusions depended on 72 anagram pairs; v3 tests 1,440 pairs and reports r=0.99 agreement, substantially addressing sensitivity to the small stimulus sample. Additional diagnostic experiments and model documentation strengthen evidence and transparency. A qualification remains: Figure 7 measures representation similarity, while its prose also claims irrecoverable CSS loss. This overinterpretation does not outweigh the substantial robustness gain.
